text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended a quiet session easier with pared losses. September shed $20 to close at $1,467 per tonne, while November closed $21 easier at $1,483 per tonne. Traders said robustas have come under pressure from Indonesian-led selling. Some traders said the market was bottoming out in the near term and that a rebound to an oversold condition could be on the cards.

Arabica futures in New York ended mostly higher in light dealings. Coffee prices defied pre-opening expectations and headed lower at the outset, pressured by commission house selling on the heels of a slightly bearish stock report from the Green Coffee Association of New York. The GCA reported stocks up 219,000 bags to 2.335 million bags which was the upper end of expectations which ranged from 50,000 to 250,000 bags. Friday's weak close in both London and New York added to the bearish tone but scale down trade support held prices even. Traders said the early pressure was mostly speculative in orientation. Liquidation of the September contract may have added pressure as well. Friday's commitment of traders report showed that as of August 12 speculators and small traders held net longs of 5,443 lots versus 4,452 in the previous COT- report. September added 2.25 cents/lb to close at 180.20 cents/lb, while December closed 1.10 cents/lb higher at 162.95 cents/lb.

UNITED STATES - US coffee roastings in the week ended August 9 totalled 395,000 bags which was equal to last year. For the year to date there were 10.510 million bags, up slightly from 10.325 million bags in 1996.
UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported exchange-certified coffee stocks rose by 457 60-kg bags as of August 15 to 92,428 bags. An additional 5,500 bags of coffee were pending grading, the exchange said.

COSTA RICA - Costa Rica's coffee crop will be around 2.5 million 60-kg bags in 1997/98 (October/September) Guillermo Canet, the executive director of the Costa Rican Coffee Institute said, up from the 2.223 million bags produced the previous year. However, only recently the Costa Rican Coffee Institute said the 1996/97 coffee campaign ended with a crop of 2.7 million 60-kg bags, similar to the last cycle.

COLOMBIA - Truck drivers of Colombia's main transport union declared a strike at the Pacific Coast port of Buenaventura in protest at low freight rates. Sources at the port, which handles about 60 per cent of all Colombia's incoming and outbound foreign trade, including key coffee exports, said operations were not affected.

GERMANY ** - Germany imported 1.255 million bags of coffee in April 1997, nearly 20 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 5.054 million bags, nearly 19 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by more than 5 per cent 13.577 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/April 1997 were El Salvador (461,000 vs 356,300 bags), Brazil (896,600 vs 137,300 bags), Colombia (832,000 vs 994,300 bags) and Vietnam (413,200 vs 280,000 bags).

The country exported 1.4 million bags of coffee in January/April 1997, 25 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose by nearly 18 per cent to 3.805 million bags.
